title: VPC upgrade orchestration: connection-draining + synthetic-health probes for zero-downtime rollouts
creator: Liam Chen
description: Design and implement an orchestrated data-plane upgrade path for Private (VPC) deployments that achieves zero-downtime for inference traffic. This ticket scopes a new upgrade strategy that combines: 1) graceful connection draining at the tenant/route level, 2) synthetic health probes that exercise both model inference and cache priming behaviors, and 3) Terraform/IaC hooks to expose drain windows and probe configuration to customer-managed stacks. Goals: maintain p99 latency SLOs, avoid lost in-flight requests, and provide deterministic rollback triggers when probes or telemetry indicate regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade process can be executed from the private control plane and via IaC-driven orchestrations (Terraform module flag) without manual node-by-node actions.
Connection draining prevents new connections and gracefully completes in-flight requests; no 5xx spike or increased 95th/99th token latency beyond defined thresholds during canary steps.

Synthetic probe suite validates: model response correctness (structured output acceptance), KV cache warmup behavior for common prefixes, and end-to-end p95 latency under a small synthetic load; failures are surfaced as rollout aborts.
Rollback triggers: probe failures, elevated error rate, or SLO regressions automatically start a deterministic rollback within the orchestrator and notify on-call and the customer control plane.
Terraform module includes config inputs to control drain_timeout, probe_frequency, probe_scenarios, and canary_batch_size with documentation and examples.
E2E smoke tests for upgrades run in CI against a staging VPC and are green in the release branch before production rollout.
Audit log entries are produced for each rollout step and included in the customer's private audit stream when enabled.
Security review completed for probes and IaC surface (no secrets exfiltration).
implementation_notes: Add a connection-drain controller in the private control plane that: tags routes/tenants for draining, marks nodes unschedulable for new streams, and exposes remaining-in-flight count via metrics.

Implement a synthetic-probe runner that lives in the control plane but executes workers within the tenant VPC (sidecar or ephemeral runner) to avoid cross-tenant network dependency and surface realistic network latencies.
Probes should include: 1) structured-output validation (JSON schema), 2) short-sequence generation to verify KV cache hits/misses, 3) latency sampling across short and medium context sizes.

Extend terraform/private-deployments module with: terraform variable inputs for drain_timeout_seconds, probe_config (list of scenarios), canary_segment_percentage, and an enable_automatic_rollback boolean. Generate example usage in README.
Orchestrator must perform staged upgrades: allocate canary subset -> drain/cycle canary nodes with probes -> evaluate metrics -> promote next wave or rollback.
Instrument additional metrics: in_flight_requests_per_tenant, drain_progress_percent, probe_pass_rate_by_scenario, cache_warm_ratio, and rollout_step_duration.
Expose a dry-run mode in the IaC module to simulate drain windows and probe failures for validation in customer CI pipelines.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Dry-run (staging): Enable terraform dry-run for a staging VPC, simulate drain windows and probe failures. Validate audit logs and telemetry.
Phase 1 - Canary (small fraction): Select 2% of tenants in a single region; mark nodes for drain, run probe suite targeting those tenants, observe for 30 minutes of steady-state.
Phase 2 - Gradual ramp: If canary passes, expand to 10% and then 30% in controlled waves with 15-minute observation windows and probe checks between waves.
Phase 3 - Full rollout: If all waves pass metrics checks, run final drain and upgrade for remaining nodes with continuous probe monitoring.
Phase 4 - Post-rollout verification: Run extended synthetic probe scenarios for 24 hours and validate cost/latency signals before marking release complete.
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback triggers: any probe scenario < 95% pass rate for > 3 consecutive probes, spike in 5xx > 0.5% above baseline, or sustained p95 token latency > baseline + 120ms for 10m.

Rollback steps: 1) Pause rollout, 2) Revert routing to previous model/node image for impacted tenants, 3) Re-enable previously drained nodes for new connections after health confirmation, 4) Run a focused probe sweep to confirm restoration.
Safety: Ensure rollback is idempotent and limited to affected region/slot; avoid global back-out unless multiple regional canaries fail.
Notifications: PagerDuty, customer control plane webhook, and internal #oncall-redwood channel with rollback reason and metrics snapshot.
test_plan: Unit tests for controller state machine: drain -> waiting-for-inflight -> probe-run -> promote/rollback transitions.
Integration test: Terraform module deploys staging VPC with probe workers; simulate a failing probe to ensure orchestrator aborts and rolls back.
Load test: Synthetic workload that simulates 5 tenants at realistic QPS to validate cache warmup and p95 during drain waves.
Chaos test: Random node reboots during drain windows to validate controller resilience and correctness of in-flight completion accounting.
Security test: Validate that probes running in-customer VPC only use ephemeral credentials and never log secrets; run static analysis on probe code.
